note: Let G act on itself by conjugation. For x in G, the stabilizer is C_G(x), so the orbit size is [G:C_G(x)]. If x is noncentral, C_G(x) is proper. Since its order divides p^n, it is p^m with 0<=m<n, hence the orbit size p^(n-m) is divisible by p. The singleton orbits are exactly elements of Z(G). Partitioning G into orbits gives |G|=|Z(G)|+sum(noncentral orbit sizes), so |Z(G)| is divisible by p. Since identity lies in Z(G), divisibility by p>=2 forces |Z(G)|>=p and hence a nonidentity element.
